correctness.rationale: Let e=||Qv||^2, w=Qv/sqrt(e), D=||Qx||^2 and c=<w,Qx>. The exact 2x2 orthogonal compression of Q is [[e,sqrt(e)c],[sqrt(e)c,D]], so the next error is its smaller eigenvalue and the normalized ratio equals 2(D-c^2)/(e+D+sqrt((D-e)^2+4ec^2)). A coupled Gaussian tangent representation yields R_e -> (Z_2^2+...+Z_m^2)/(Z_1^2+...+Z_m^2) almost surely. Independent chi-squares give Beta((m-1)/2,1/2). Since 0<=R_e<=1, bounded convergence supplies the stated moments. O(r)xO(m) invariance and e_next<=e prove conditional-kernel convergence and the fixed-k iid-product law by induction. Actual standalone verify.py executed with 1,851 successful exact matrix and numerical distribution checks; finite checks are corroboration and do not replace the analytic limit proof.

value.rationale: Repeated largest eigenvalues are a natural degenerate spectral regime explicitly excluded by the motivating simple-top spectral-gap rate theorem. The exact beta distribution yields an entire local one-step reliability CDF, all positive moments, and fixed-horizon product behavior, with a surprising dependence only on the dimension of the complement. This is an exact useful classification and benchmark rather than a routine restatement of simple-eigenvalue convergence or a single numerical test.
